Text Hierarchy Tips for Social Graphics

  • Headline (48-72px): Your main message. Use bold, high-contrast colors. Keep it short — 3-6 words for thumbnails, 6-10 for feed posts.
  • Subheading (28-40px): Supporting text. Place below the headline. Use a lighter weight or smaller size to create visual hierarchy.
  • CTA / URL (18-24px): Call-to-action like "Shop Now" or "Link in Bio". Place at the bottom and keep it legible on mobile.
  • Shadow & Outline: Use text shadow for readability over busy backgrounds. Use outline (stroke) for a bold promotional look. Combine both for high-impact YouTube thumbnails.
  • Color Contrast: White text over dark backgrounds or dark text over light sections. Never place text on high-detail areas without shadow support.

When to Use Each Format

  • Instagram Post (1:1): Feed posts, brand announcements, quotes. The square format works everywhere on Instagram and looks great in grid previews.
  • Instagram Story / Reel (9:16): Full-screen mobile content, time-sensitive announcements, behind-the-scenes, short video covers.
  • Facebook Post (1.9:1 / 1200×630): Standard link shares, blog post promotion, event announcements. This is the most commonly shared format across the web.
  • Facebook Cover (2.63:1): Your Facebook page header. Avoid critical content near the edges — profile picture and CTA button overlay on mobile.
  • Twitter/X Post (16:9): Shared images in the timeline. Wide format performs well for screenshots, infographics, and visual tweets.
  • LinkedIn Banner (4:1): Professional profile header. Keep it clean and minimal — your headline and photo overlay on the left.
  • YouTube Thumbnail (16:9): The most important design element for video click-through rate. Use bold text (large font), high contrast, faces/emotions, and bright colors.
  • TikTok Video (9:16): Vertical full-screen covers. Text should be large and centered. Leave room for captions and UI elements at top and bottom.
  • Pinterest Pin (2:3 / 1000×1500): Tall vertical images perform best. Use vertical flow, soft colors, and inspirational text. Add your brand logo at the bottom.

guide_html:
What Is Photo Restoration?

Old photos degrade over time. Scratches from physical handling, dust embedded in the emulsion, fading from UV exposure, and noise from low-quality scanning all damage the image. Photo restoration is the process of reversing or mitigating these defects to reveal the original image beneath.

Our tool applies four core algorithms, all running locally in your browser with zero uploads:

  • Denoising (Median Filter) — A 3×3 convolution that replaces each pixel with the median value of its neighbors. This smooths out random grain and sensor noise while preserving edges far better than a blur filter.
  • Scratch Removal (Adaptive Detection + Inpainting) — Analysis that detects outlier pixels — thin, high-contrast linear defects typical of scratches — and replaces them with averaged neighbor values (inpainting).
  • Contrast Enhancement (Histogram Stretching) — Spreads the pixel intensity range to use the full 0–255 spectrum, recovering detail lost in faded or washed-out photos.
  • Sharpen (Unsharp Mask) — A blurred copy of the image is subtracted from the original to find edges, which are then amplified for a crisper appearance.

When to Use Each Restoration Technique

  • Denoise — Use on grainy photos, low-light shots, or scanned film with visible silver grain. Start at 30–50 and increase until the grain is smoothed. At very high values (80+), fine details may soften.
  • Scratch Removal — Essential for scanned prints or negatives with surface scratches. Works by detecting narrow, high-contrast lines and filling them. Best at 40–70. Very deep scratches may require additional manual touch-up.
  • Contrast Boost — Ideal for faded, hazy, or underexposed old photos. Histogram stretching recovers detail in shadows and highlights. Start at 30 and adjust; over-boosting creates harsh, unnatural contrast.
  • Sharpen — Use after denoising to bring back crispness in faces and text. Max out around 50–70 for most scanned photos. Very old photos with heavy damage may look unnatural if oversharpened.
  • Brightness — Adjust the overall exposure. Positive values lighten; negative values darken. Use before contrast adjustment for best results.
  • Warmth / Sepia — Adds a classic sepia tone by adjusting the red/blue channel balance. Use at 20–50 for a subtle vintage warmth, or 70–100 for a strong antique sepia look. Excellent for black-and-white portraits.
💡 Pro Tip: Always start with Auto Restore. It applies all techniques with balanced values. Then fine-tune individual sliders — never adjust more than 2–3 parameters at once to maintain a natural look.

Understanding How Each Algorithm Works

Median Filter Denoising: The algorithm examines every pixel and its 8 immediate neighbors (a 3×3 window). Instead of averaging them (which blurs edges), it sorts the 9 values and picks the median. This removes salt-and-pepper noise and grain while keeping edges sharp. Unlike Gaussian blur, median filtering preserves fine lines and textures.

Adaptive Scratch Detection: The tool scans each row for pixels that deviate significantly from their horizontal neighbors — a signature of thin scratches. When an outlier is found (pixel value differing by more than a threshold from its neighbors), it's replaced with the average of the 4 surrounding pixels. The threshold adapts based on local contrast so textured areas aren't falsely detected as scratches.

Histogram Stretching (Contrast): The tool computes the minimum and maximum intensity values across all channels. It then remaps the entire range so the darkest pixel becomes 0 and the brightest becomes 255. This recovers hidden detail in faded photos. A clip percentage (typically 0.5%) avoids extreme outliers from skewing the stretch.

Unsharp Mask (Sharpen): A Gaussian-blurred copy of the image is created. The blurred version is subtracted from the original to isolate edge information (the "mask"). This mask is scaled and added back to the original, amplifying transitions between light and dark areas. The result: edges look crisper without adding noise to flat areas.

Scanning Tips for Best Results

The quality of your restoration depends heavily on the input scan. Follow these tips for the best results:

  • Scan at 600 DPI or higher. Low-resolution scans lose detail that cannot be recovered. 600 DPI is ideal for prints; use 1200+ DPI for small photos (e.g., 2×3 inches).
  • Use a flatbed scanner, not a phone camera. Phone cameras introduce perspective distortion, lens flare, and uneven lighting. A flatbed scanner gives consistent, flat illumination.
  • Clean the photo first. Gently wipe the surface with a microfiber cloth. For stubborn dust, use compressed air. Never use wet cleaners on old photos — the emulsion may be water-soluble.
  • Avoid flash when photographing old photos. If scanning isn't an option and you must use a phone, photograph in indirect natural light with the photo lying flat. Angle the camera carefully to avoid reflections.
  • Save scans as PNG (lossless). For archiving, always save your scan as PNG. JPEG compression introduces artifacts that make restoration harder. Use JPEG only if file size is a concern.
  • Scan in color even for B&W photos. Scanning black-and-white photos in color preserves the full tonal range and allows you to apply sepia tones later. Convert to grayscale only if color casts are severe.
  • Handle with care. Old photos are fragile. Wear cotton gloves if possible. Handle by the edges only. If the photo is curled, place it under a flat weight for a few hours before scanning.
💡 Key Point: A good scan at 600 DPI with even lighting is the single most important factor in restoration quality. No algorithm can recover detail that was never captured. Invest time in getting the scan right.

Why 100% Browser-Based Matters

Traditional photo restoration tools require expensive software like Adobe Photoshop or dedicated restoration plugins. Online services often upload your photos to external servers, raising privacy concerns. Our approach is different:

  • No uploads. Your photo never leaves your device. All processing happens in the browser via the Canvas 2D API.
  • No signup. No accounts, no emails, no tracking. Just upload and restore.
  • No file size limits imposed by servers. The only limit is your browser's memory. We recommend 20MB as a practical maximum.
  • Instant processing. No waiting for uploads or server queues. Results are rendered in milliseconds.
  • Privacy guaranteed. Since nothing is transmitted, your family photos, historical documents, and sensitive images remain completely private.

This makes SmartImgKit's photo restoration tool ideal for restoring personal family photos, historical documents, and archive materials where privacy matters.

📷 Step 1: Take a Good Portrait Photo

The quality of your final ID photo depends heavily on the source image. For best results, follow these tips:

Stand against a plain, light-colored wall (white or off-white works best). Make sure your face is centered in the frame and both ears are visible. Use even, soft lighting — natural window light from the front is ideal. Avoid harsh overhead lights that cast shadows under your eyes, nose, and chin. If wearing glasses, check that there is no glare on the lenses. Some countries require glasses to be removed entirely for ID photos.

Remove headwear such as hats, caps, or scarves unless worn for religious or medical reasons. Keep a neutral expression with your mouth closed and both eyes open, looking directly at the camera. Take the photo from straight on — your head should not be tilted or turned.

🌍 Step 2: Select Your Country and Photo Type

Browse the country list below the upload area and click on the photo type you need. Each country has specific size requirements measured in millimeters (mm) or inches. The tool automatically crops your photo to the correct aspect ratio for the selected standard.

Popular passport and visa standards:

  • 🇺🇸 US Passport — 2 × 2 inches (51 × 51 mm), white background. Same size for US Visa, Green Card, and Driver License.
  • 🇬🇧 UK Passport — 35 × 45 mm, light gray background. UK Visa and BRP use 35 × 45 mm with white background.
  • 🇨🇳 China Passport — 33 × 48 mm, white background. China ID Card 26 × 32 mm (white or blue for 2nd Gen), Driver License 22 × 32 mm.
  • 🇪🇺 Schengen Visa — 35 × 45 mm, light background. Same size for Germany, France, Italy, Spain, and Netherlands passports.
  • 🇮🇳 India Passport — 35 × 50 mm, white background. Aadhaar is 35 × 35 mm square, PAN Card is 25 × 25 mm.
  • 🇨🇦 Canada Passport — 50 × 70 mm, white background (larger than most). Canada Visa is 35 × 45 mm.
  • 🇯🇵 Japan Passport — 35 × 45 mm, white background. Japan Visa uses the same dimensions.
  • 🇲🇽 Mexico Passport — 25 × 32 mm, white background (child-like proportion).
  • 🇧🇷 Brazil Passport — 35 × 45 mm, white background.
  • 🇦🇺 Australia Passport — 35 × 45 mm, white background.
  • 🇰🇷 South Korea Passport — 35 × 45 mm, white background.
  • 🇷🇺 Russia Passport — 35 × 45 mm, white background.
  • Custom Size — Enter any width and height manually if your country is not listed.

If your specific ID type is not listed, use the Custom Size option at the bottom of the country list and enter the exact dimensions required by your application.

🎨 Step 3: Choose the Right Background Color

Different ID documents require different background colors. Our tool lets you select from five preset colors or pick a custom color:

  • White (#ffffff) — The most common background for passports and visas worldwide. Used by US, India, Canada, Japan, Australia, Schengen, Brazil, South Korea, Russia, and most other countries.
  • Blue (#3b82f6) — Required for Chinese 2nd generation ID cards (shenfenzheng) and Chinese residence permits. Also used for driver's licenses in many US states.
  • Red (#ef4444) — Used for some Chinese official documents, professional certificates, and certain visa photos.
  • Gray (#9ca3af) — Required specifically for UK passport photos. Light gray backgrounds are also accepted for some Schengen visa applications.
  • Green (#22c55e) — Occasionally used for specific official documents and professional applications in some jurisdictions.

The AI background removal engine processes your photo and replaces the original background cleanly. The result is a professional, uniform background color that meets official requirements.

⬇️ Step 4: Generate and Download Your ID Photo

Once you've uploaded your photo, selected the country standard, and chosen your background color, click the "Generate ID Photo" button. The tool will:

  1. Run AI background removal to extract the subject from the original background
  2. Composite the subject onto your chosen background color
  3. Crop the image to the exact aspect ratio of your selected country standard
  4. Render the final image at 300 DPI for high-quality printing

Processing typically takes 3–10 seconds depending on your device. The AI model runs entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded to any server. After processing, click "Download" to save the PNG file. You can then print it at any photo kiosk or load it into an online application.

📋 Photo Requirements Checklist

Before taking your ID photo, review this checklist to ensure it meets official standards:

  • Front-facing with both eyes visible and open — no side profiles or closed eyes
  • Neutral expression with mouth closed — no smiling, frowning, or raised eyebrows
  • Plain white or off-white background — no patterns, textures, or objects behind you
  • Even lighting — no shadows on your face, behind your head, or on the background
  • Head centered and upright — not tilted, turned, or rotated in any direction
  • No hats or head coverings — except for religious, cultural, or medical reasons documented in advance
  • No glasses if possible — if required, ensure no glare, heavy frames blocking eyes, or tinted lenses
  • Recent photo — taken within the last 6 months for most passport and visa applications
  • High resolution — at least 600 × 600 pixels recommended; 1200 × 1200 or higher is ideal
  • Both ears visible — hair should be pulled back if it covers the ears
  • No other people or objects visible in the frame — only the applicant should appear
  • Properly exposed — not too dark (underexposed) or too bright (overexposed, blown-out highlights)

guide_html:
Why White Backgrounds Matter for E-Commerce

Online marketplaces like Amazon, eBay, and Google Shopping have specific requirements for product images. Amazon's main image policy requires a pure white background that blends with the page — no watermarks, logos, or props. White backgrounds increase conversion rates by making products the clear focal point and reducing visual distractions. Studies show that products with professional white-background photos see up to 30% higher click-through rates than those with busy backgrounds.

Tips for Great Product Photos

Even Lighting: Use diffused lighting from both sides to eliminate harsh shadows on the product itself. Soft, even lighting makes the background removal process more accurate and yields a cleaner final result. Avoid direct flash or overhead lighting that creates hotspots.

Clean Background: Start with a solid, contrasting background color — white, gray, or black — to give the AI the best chance of accurately identifying the product edges. Avoid patterns, textures, or gradients that can confuse the segmentation model.

Sharp Focus: Ensure your product is in sharp focus. Blurry product images result in fuzzy edges after background removal. Use a tripod for consistent sharpness across batch shoots and focus on the front-facing product details.

Multiple Angles: Photograph your product from multiple angles: front, side, back, and detail shots. Batch processing makes it easy to apply the same white background to all angles for a consistent listing appearance. Amazon recommends at least five different product angles for an optimized listing.

Avoid Overlapping: When photographing products, avoid overlapping items. The AI works best on individual products with clear, unobstructed boundaries. Photograph items separately and use our Image Merger tool to create group shots later.

E-Commerce Platform Background Requirements

Amazon: Main images require pure white background (RGB 255, 255, 255). The image must show only the product, no accessories or props unless included. Minimum 1000px on the longest side for zoom functionality.

Shopify: White backgrounds are recommended for a clean, professional storefront. No strict requirement but consistent white backgrounds create a premium brand experience.

eBay: Gallery images perform best with white backgrounds. eBay's search algorithm favors clear, high-contrast product images against clean backgrounds.

Etsy: Clean white backgrounds help your products stand out in category pages and search results. Etsy's style guide recommends consistent backgrounds across your shop.

Google Shopping: Requires product to fill at least 75% of the image frame with a clean, unobtrusive background. White background images consistently achieve higher approval rates.

How the Background Removal Technology Works

This tool uses @imgly/background-removal (v1.7.0), a state-of-the-art AI model based on the REMBG architecture running entirely in your browser via WebAssembly. The model uses a deep neural network trained on millions of images to accurately segment subjects from their backgrounds. When you select a background color, the tool composites the extracted product onto the chosen color using the alpha channel, ensuring smooth edges and no white halos.

Key benefits of browser-based processing: your product images never leave your device, there are no file size limits imposed by server uploads, and processing is free with no usage caps. The first load downloads the AI model (approximately 40MB), but subsequent runs are instant as the model is cached by your browser.
